`AUTH_REQUIRED` is not `UNA
UTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a different\nkey will not help. Complete the OAuth flow for that server yourself, upload t

## Rate limits

Each key gets **60 requests per minute** sustained, with bursts up to **10**.
Exce

eding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in
seconds):

```http theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
HTT

P/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code": "RATE_LIMITED", "message": "API key rate limit exceeded. Slow down

and retry." }
```

Honor `Retry-After`, add jittered exponential backoff, and expect these limits
to be tuned during the pre

view.

Other `429`s — the per-minute brakes and daily budgets described with the
endpoints below — carry `Retry-After` whenever
the refusal knows when it\nlifts, which is the ordinary case. Treat it as a hint that is usually there\nrather than a guarantee:

a refusal that reaches you without one still needs
your backoff, so **never** block waiting for a header that may not come.

##

Endpoints

Each endpoint is fully documented — request and response schemas, examples,
and an interactive playground — under *

*Endpoints** in the sidebar.

**Catalog** — discover the IDs everything else takes:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
|
`GET /me` | The account behind the key |\n| `GET /organizations` | The organizations the caller belongs to — where `organizationI
d` comes from. A key is bound to one organization and only ever sees that one |\n| `GET /projects` | Projects the key can access (
optionally `?organizationId=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers` | The project's saved MCP servers |\n| `GET /projects/{pro
jectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions` | A server's stored revisions, newest first: captures of its tools and server info, recorded
whenever they change (`?limit=&cursor=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}` | One rev
ision: every tool's definition and the server info it reported. Fields listed in `droppedFields` were too large to store, so they
are unknown, not absent |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/diff` | What changed since t
he revision before, or since `?from=`: tools added, removed and changed, and server info changes with both values. A field listed
in `droppedFields.from` or `droppedFields.to` was not stored on that side, so a change to it is unknown |\n| `GET /projects/{proje
ctId}/eval-suites` | The project's eval suites, with latest-run summaries |\n| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients` | List
clients, or create one from a template or full config |\n| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}` | Read,
edit, or delete a client. The path segment takes a client **name or ID** |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}/server
s` | Replace the client's server attachments (a replacement — omitted servers are detached) |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clien
ts/{client}/duplicate` | Copy a client's current config into a new client |\n| `GET /chat-sessions` | Chat sessions (`?projectId=&

status=&limit=&before=`) |

**Project environments** — the named execution bundles (one host, optionally a
standalone server gr
oup, optionally pinned skills and plugin versions) that eval\nsuites and goals run against. Reads need project membership; **every
write\nneeds project admin**. Writes are revisioned: pass the `revision` you last read\nback as `expectedRevision`, and a stale v

alue returns `CONFLICT` (409) instead
of overwriting a concurrent edit.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET`, `POST
/projects/{projectId}/environments` | List environments (`?includeArchived=true` to include archived ones), or create one |\n| `G
ET`, `PATCH /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}` | Read one environment, or edit it (send `null` to clear `serverAt
tachmentId`, `skillSelection`, or `pluginVersionIds`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` | Prev
iew the host config, closed server set, and pinned plugin versions this environment resolves to right now |\n| `POST /projects/{pr
ojectId}/environments/{environmentId}/archive` | Archive it — reversible, and frees the name for a new one |\n| `POST /projects/{p
rojectId}/environments/{environmentId}/restore` | Restore an archived environment |\n\nArchive and restore are explicit sub-action
s rather than a `DELETE` because the\nrow is kept and restore has real semantics: it re-checks the name and drops\nplugin pins who

se version no longer exists.

| Endpoin

t | What it does |

| `POST .../validate` | Connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot |
| `POST .../docto
r` | Full health workflow: probe → connect → initialize → capabilities |\n| `POST .../check-oauth` | Does this server require an O
Auth grant? |\n| `POST .../tools` | List the server's tools |\n| `POST .../tools/call` | Execute a tool; returns the MCP `CallTool
Result` plus additive `durationMs`, and `authChallenge` when the result asks for sign-in (see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challe
nges)) |\n| `POST .../prompts` | List the server's prompts |\n| `POST .../prompts/get` | Render a prompt; returns the MCP `GetProm
ptResult` verbatim |\n| `POST .../resources` | List the server's resources |\n| `POST .../resources/read` | Read one resource by U
RI |\n| `POST .../export` | One JSON snapshot of tools, resources, and prompts |\n| `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE .../accounts[/{

**Eval runs** (`/projects/{projectId}/...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-suites` | Author-on
ly: create a suite + its test cases from `name` + `serverIds` + a default `model` + `tests`, WITHOUT running it; responds `201` +
`suiteId`. Each test's case body is an ordered `steps` array (prompt / toolCall / interact / assert); per-test `model`/`provider`/
`runs` are optional and fall back to suite defaults |\n| `POST .../eval-runs` | Create a run from a `suiteId` (rerun; `serverIds`
optional — defaults to the suite's saved servers) or `suiteName` + inline `tests` + `serverIds` (new suite). `environmentId` (requ
ires `suiteId`) runs against one of the suite's attached environments instead. Responds `202` + `runId` |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suite
s/{suiteId}` | Edit suite settings, including `environmentIds` — the project environments the suite runs against (non-empty array
sets/replaces, `null` clears) |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/schedule` | Enable/disable scheduled runs; `environmentId` pin
s which environment they launch |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` | Run status, result, and summary — poll until terminal. Carries
`gateWaiver`: the audited override in force over this run's gate, or `null` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate` | The stored sui
te quality-gate report for this run (`passed` / `failed` / `non_gateable` / `not_configured`). `not_configured` is a 200 report, n
ever a missing route. A deployment that predates the evaluator answers `422 FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}
/decision-summary` | **Start here when a run did not pass.** The canonical run decision contract: the verdict and where it came fr
om, counts labelled with the population they count, the run's own verdict decision, and per-trial diagnostics with the user-value
chain, the first failed stage, the failure category, evidence scoped to that stage, and one next action (paginated) |\n| `POST ...
/eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | Override a **failing** run's release gate until `expiresAt` (required, future, max 30 days out)
, with a `reason` (required, max 500 chars). Manage tier. Does NOT change the run's `result` — the run keeps its verdict and the w
